Specie.Explanation: "Bjornling Norse are the most outward-looking of the Norse, trading along the coasts of the Sea of Claws."
"Sarl Norse range east towards Kislev, and are as at home on horseback as aboard a longship."

"Skaeling Norse are the most openly devoted to the Ruinous Powers, Khorne foremost among them. A Skaeling Character who generates the Pure Soul Talent as a Random Talent may take the Mark of Khorne instead."

"A player may like to create a Norse Dwarf Character from one of the Krakas. If so, these rules can be used rather than the rules for Dwarfs on page 36 of the WFRP Core Rulebook. Norse Dwarfs are generally thought easygoing by Dwarf standards, but they still record their grievances and seek recompense for them."

Talent.Explanation: "This Talent allows a Character to learn a chanty (see page 67). Whenever a Character buys a new level in the Talent they learn a new song. A Chanty affects an entire crew. To use the talent the Chantyman should find a location within earshot of as many of the crew as possible and pass an Entertain (Singing) Test. It takes 30 seconds for a Chantyman to establish the chanty, after which the effect lasts for three minutes plus a number of minutes equal to the SL on the Entertain (Singing) Test. The only combat action the Chantyman can make while the Chanty is being performed is a Dodge. Other actions can be made at the GM’s discretion, such as Perception Tests or Cool Tests. If the Chantyman takes damage or fails any Opposed Test their Chanty ends. A Chanty may be sung at each watch. There’s only so much inspiration a crew can take."

"You are respected and trusted by your crew. Any appropriate Leadership Test on board your ship or involving your crew gains an SL bonus equal to your levels in Master and Commander. This bonus applies to Crew Tests as well as individual Leadership Tests."

Career.Explanation: "You scour the local beaches for anything of value, always on the lookout for a hidden gem or lucky find. Beachcombers live by their wits upon the littoral, finding most of what they need to survive through Manann’s providence. A diverse range of flotsam and jetsam gets washed up on the beaches of the Sea of Claws, and Beachcombers take full advantage of this. Almost any item that can be traded will find itself aboard a ship on the Sea of Claws, and therefore, provided it floats for a time, could end up washed up on a beach. Such castaway cargo can often fetch good money from a local merchant or be bartered for other useful stuff."

"You coordinate the actions of your ship’s crew, guide their activity, and raise their morale with rousing ditties. Any sailor worth their salt performs better to the sound of a Chantyman. Some say they are just singers and musicians, like any others. However, it is a common belief amongst most ships crews that the best Chantymen can have an unnatural effect upon the crew."

"You guide ships through the most treacherous waters of the world’s several seas. Huffers are known to work on the rivers of the Empire, but pilots and navigators are obviously even more invaluable to captains of ocean-going vessels. Not only is knowledge of areas of rock, reef, or sandbank necessary, but seafarers often sail beyond sight of any landmark, so navigators at sea must display practical knowledge of how to pinpoint their location from the position of the sun and the stars."

"You command a ship, and must inspire your crew to place their lives in your hands. Ship’s Officers, especially captains, are judge, jury, and executioner aboard their vessels. They have Manann-given power of life and death over the crew, but this is a double-edged sword. The Officer must also inspire the crew to trust their judgement and competence, or the hands might mutiny."

"You work on board a ship, keeping the decks clean and the sails suitably trimmed. Humans of the Old World had to learn the skills of sailing for themselves, for the Dwarfs were never a great maritime civilisation, and the Elves had no desire to encourage Human exploration of the wider world. Human civilisation before the age of Sigmar rarely ventured upon the waves. Even the mighty Khemrians built few vessels capable of ocean travel."

"You bring the will of Manann to his followers and intercede to court his favour and avoid his wrath. Priests of Manann are found working and ministering on board vessels as often as they are found in his temples and shrines. Manann is a fickle and moody deity, but he seems to respect a degree of practical ability and experience of the seas in his priests, and most of them spend a part of their career at sea."

"You maintain and fire the guns aboard ship and are expert in their use. The Ship’s Gunner is part of the crew, and just like any other crew member they are expected to help with the sailing of their vessel and to put their hand to anything involved in running the ship. In addition, they are experts on blackpowder weapons and their use at sea."

"You lure vessels to a watery doom and make off with their precious cargo. Bands of wreckers work around the coasts of all the nations of the Old World. They live by salvaging cargos from stricken vessels. Although there are some wreckers who live by treacherous lengths of coastline and wait patiently for ships to run aground, they may even manage to keep on the right side of the law as they do so, informing the authorities of their actions but seeking a cut of the salvage. But such people are not archetypal wreckers. The enterprise of wrecking is usually an opportunistic and criminal one, and the name is associated with those who take an active role in ensuring a steady supply of ships to wreck and plunder."

Item.name: Fleet of Riverboats and Wrecker Crew

Career.Explanation: "You preach that the strong have the right to take advantage of the weak and call on Stromfels to aid you in your predations. Priests of Stromfels are actively involved in the business of piracy, raiding, or wrecking — to do less would be hypocrisy. You may not take the Priest of Stromfels as your first career, and it can only be undertaken after you have completed the first tier of a predatory occupation. This need not be a seafaring career; there are Outlaws, Protagonists, and Racketeers who might find much to admire in Stromfels, but most of his priests have either served as crew on a pirate vessel, or worked as Wreckers. ‘Feel that sou-wester blowing up? There’ll be gifts from Stromfels scattered on the shore tomorrow morning, and a few more souls in his jaws this night.’ — Thijs Vroom, Marienburg sailor"

Sort.Explanation: "This Miracle may be performed whenever it is time for a ship to calculate Manann’s Mood. You perform the rites thought best to supplicate Manann. His mood improves by 2d10, –1 for each Sin Point you currently have."

"Upon completing the invocation, an albatross descends from the clouds and follows the ship. The albatross waits up to 1 hour for the ship to sail, and after that, it stays with the ship until the duration expires. As long as the albatross is present, the ship cannot sink, no matter how much damage it takes. Should the albatross be killed, the ship suffers from –d10 Morale and –2d10 for Manann’s Mood (should you need statistics for an albatross, treat it as a pigeon from WFRP, page 316, though its Size is Small and it has 3 Wounds)."
"Your blessing grants a character an instinctive feel for the sea and sailing. Any Row, Sail, or Swim Tests they make benefit from +1 SL."

"Your prayers allow a character to breathe water as if it were air. When it comes to drowing in water, the character can ignore the Suffocation rules on WFRP page 181 for the duration of the Miracle. It is not possible to perform this Miracle while your own mouth is underwater."
"You can chant this prayer, quelling a strong current. The M rating of a strait or whirlpool is reduced to 0 whilst the miracle is in effect."

"You call doom down on the enemies of Manann. Provided the targeted ship is crewed by those who do not warrant the respect of Manann (followers of Chaos, worshippers of Stromfels, Orcs and Goblins, Skaven, crews who have a negative Manann’s Mood score), that crew suffer from a curse. Add 2 to the Damage of all hits the crew receives whilst the Miracle is in effect."

"You can chant this prayer to a sea creature, causing it to forget all rage and hunger whilst the miracle is in effect. For the duration of the miracle the creature will not make any hostile actions, provided that it suffers no damage or adverse Conditions."
Sort.Target: "1 creature with the Aquatic or the Marine Trait"

Sort.Explanation: "You can chant this prayer at a ship you can see. The ship suffers –1 M and –1 SL to Man."

"When trying to track someone who has been injured, you smell the smallest drops of blood even if some attempt has been made to remove them. You can follow their trail over land and water by passing an Easy (+40) Track Test."

"You inflict nightmares upon your target that make it impossible for them to get a good night’s sleep, resulting in lethargy and weakness. The nightmares are extremely vivid, disturbing, and connected to the ocean in some way; they commonly involve a woman draped in fronds of bloodwrack walking from the sea to torment the victim. Whilst under the influence of the Miracle the target must pass a Difficult (–10) Cool Test every time they take some rest to recover from Fatigued Conditions. If the Test is failed, the Fatigued Condition remains."

"You proclaim that Stromfels is the true lord of the sea, and that the superstitions of those who respect Manann are delusions. Once the miracle is in effect, roll on the table below and apply the result to the Manann’s Mood score for the ship you are currently aboard (see page 130). Add 1 to the roll for every Sin Point you possess. d10 Roll Result : - 1 to 4 Stromfels Triumphant! Whilst the miracle is in effect, treat Manann’s Mood as 0. - 5 to 8 Stromfels Ascends! Roll 5d10. The number may be added to Manann’s Mood if it is currently negative, or subtracted from it if it is positive. - 9 No effect. Manann’s Mood is calculated as normal. - 10 or more Manann Provoked! Roll 5d10, he number is subtracted from Manann’s Mood."
"You command the sea to form a massive wave that crashes into a specific target, such as a person in the water or on the shore, a boat, or a lighthouse. The wave counts as having a CR of 15."
"You curse someone, even the saltiest of seadogs, with a bout of seasickness that lasts for one hour. See page 125 for details of Seasickness."

"You focus on a stricken vessel, exerting your will to ensure that none escape. Splits and tears in the target ship’s hull widen as a result of the miracle. Double the target ship’s Holed Rating (see page 117)."

"You call the winds to blow with greater force into the sails of 1 ship. Increase the intensity of the wind by 1 step for the duration of the miracle (see page 107). The direction of the wind is not affected."

"Facing a ship at sea, you produce a stream of seaweed. The slimy algae surrounds the vessel, which becomes enmeshed. Whilst caught in the mire the vessel suffers -2 to its Movement Characteristic, and adjusts its Manoeuvre Characteristic by -3 SL. A crew can be ordered to cut the ship free with an Extended Challenging (+0) Boat Handling Test, to a target number equal to the caster's Willpower Bonus + SLs."
"You gather Ghyran from the sea, taking small amounts of water with it. Cleansed of impurities, this water flows to the ship's stores, replenishing any empty barrels of water."

"You pull on the Ghyran surrounding the target area, moving it around and around. The water starts to churn, and a whirlpool forms in the target area. Whirlpools are described on page 114 of Sea of Claws. The spell creates an area of Gentle Rotation, but SL can be spent on making the whirlpool larger as per the Overcasting rules : 5 SL Whirlpool, 8 SL Powerful Vortex, 13 SL A Maelstrom, 21 SL or more The Maelstrom."

"This spell must be cast while on a journey with a set destination, the location of which is known to the caster. Closing your eyes, you focus your Second Sight on the heavens, tracing Azyr's path as it crackles across the sky, seeming to jump from star to star. For an instant a bolt of Azyr connects you to your destination, leaving a shimmering blue afterimage in your vision. For the duration of the spell, all Navigation Tests made by the wizard (or involving the wizard, in the case of Crew Tests) benefit from +2 SL."

"This spell is a variation of one created by Lord Astromancer Wilfried-Gotthelm Niezlib, who sought to use it to prove his theories about the movement of celestial objects. He later realised it had more practical applications, and modified it to determine the exact moment a ship should fire a broadside. The caster can calculate the roll of the ship, distance to the target, weight of the cannonballs, and the power of each shot. For the duration of the spell, Tests made to fire a cannon benefit from +1 SL."

"You call on everyone on your vessel to be quiet, then close your eyes. An eerie silence envelops first your ship, then the surrounding sea. The sails go slack and the waves calm. The Doldrums effect from the Wind Effect Table (Sea of Claws page 107) applies for the duration of the spell."
